title: Fix PrerequisiteAnalyzer#detect_cycle false-positive: replace depth-limit short-circuit with tri-color DFS (Fowler F-finding-1)
description: Fowler permission-analyzer review (010-AT-REVW-martin-fowler-wild-permission-analyzer-2026-05-29.md) finding 1 + 10 (most-costly-to-recover-from). lib/wild/analyzers/permission/analyzers/prerequisite_analyzer.rb:56 — detect_cycle returns a fake cycle path [name, '...'] for ANY acyclic chain deeper than max_prerequisite_depth (default 10), producing a false :circular_prerequisite/critical finding. 'A security-audit gem that invents critical findings teaches operators to ignore critical findings.' Also: path-local visited (visited + [name]) + per-node re-entry in circular_findings re-discovers each real cycle N times (duplicate findings). Fix: proper tri-color DFS (white/gray/black global state), cut the depth limit entirely (it is the symptom, not a safety feature), dedupe so each cycle reported once. Beck+Fowler gate: failing unit spec 'long acyclic chain -> zero :circular_prerequisite findings' FIRST, then fix, plus integration test in full_audit_spec proving a deep acyclic chain produces zero critical findings. Owner: Role 6.
close_reason: detect_cycle false-positive fixed + merged to main via PR #33 (commit f6ff94f). Replaced the depth-limit short-circuit (fabricated :circular_prerequisite/critical for any acyclic chain deeper than max_prerequisite_depth) with iterative tri-color DFS (WHITE/GRAY/BLACK, explicit frame stack, no depth ceiling). Back-edge-to-GRAY is the only cycle signal; each ring reported once via rotation-invariant signature. Depth limit removed (Fowler finding 10). 5 failing-first specs (15-deep acyclic guard incl low-knob, 2/3-node + self-loop dedup, diamond) + full_audit integration test. martin-fowler-reviewer VERDICT: SIGN — 'disease excised, not relabeled'; walked a->b->a, 3-node, diamond, self-loop, figure-eight, dedup collisions all correct. title: Corpus-driven matcher smoke spec: assert every wildcard_corpus matches[] is true + non_matches[] is false in BOTH namespaces
description: Fowler-reviewer PR-D note: both Wild::Analyzers::Permission and Wild::CapabilityGate MUST load lib/wild/schemas/wildcard_corpus.yml at boot and run a smoke spec asserting every entry's matches[] returns true and every non_matches[] returns false against their matcher. This is the contract test that converts PR-D from 'shared data' to 'anti-drift fence.' Without it F4 is paper. Special case: negation entries (!User::Admin) have matches: [] by design — smoke harness needs an explicit branch to skip the matches[] loop and only assert non_matches[]. Source: martin-fowler-reviewer Gate 1 sign-off on PR #15.
notes: BLOCKED — design reconciliation required before this smoke spec can be written as passing. Concrete finding: wildcard_corpus.yml (Role 4 PR-D, Fowler-signed) specifies a ::-segmented grammar with 8 forms + segment-boundary semantics (User::* = direct child only; *::Admin = single-parent; User::** = recursive; !negation; middle-*). The SHIPPED matchers do NOT implement this: (1) Wild::Analyzers::Permission::Analyzers::WildcardMatcher uses a .-dotted naive glob (*->. *) with zero segment awareness — User::* matches User::Profile::Email (corpus wants false), *::Admin matches User::Settings::Admin (corpus wants false). (2) Wild::CapabilityGate has NO capability-wildcard matcher — grant.rb grants_capability? is exact-match; * only on caller identity. (3) Real capability names are dotted (admin.jobs.view) / flat (basic_introspection), not ::-segmented. A corpus-driven smoke spec would fail across the board, documenting drift rather than fencing it. Surfaced to user/architect 2026-05-31 — needs decision (see wild-<reconciliation bead>) before 1.2.1 can proceed.
close_reason: Delivered in PR #34 (merged d7f2de4): spec/wild/analyzers/permission/analyzers/wildcard_corpus_matcher_spec.rb loads lib/wild/schemas/wildcard_corpus.yml and runs Wild::Analyzers::Permission::Analyzers::WildcardMatcher.matches? against every entry, asserting all matches[]->true and all non_matches[]->false. title: Decide the fail-closed posture for ALLOW results when both the audit writer and logger are dark
description: Armstrong F2 gate, most-costly-to-recover-from finding on wild-rvv.4.1.1. emit_audit rescues write failures -> log_audit_failure -> which rescues logger failures -> returns nil. The terminal silent path requires BOTH the audit writer AND the configured logger to be broken simultaneously (pinned by audit_liveness_spec). That bound is honest, but for a SECURITY gate the posture is wrong for ALLOW results: today an ALLOW still returns successfully even when the gate could neither write the audit nor log the audit-failure -> a privileged action proceeds with zero record the gate ever weighed in. A denial nobody saw is recoverable (action blocked); an ALLOW nobody saw is not (action already happened, unrecorded). DECIDE: when emit_audit cannot write AND cannot log, for an ALLOW result the gate should either (a) degrade to DENY (fail closed — 'if you cannot prove you decided safely, do not let the action proceed'), or (b) surface an audit_degraded flag on the result the caller can refuse to honor. Denials in the same dark-audit state are tolerable as-is. This is a contract change -> own design + spec, do not fold into a test bead. Source: joe-armstrong-reviewer SIGN-OFF on PR for wild-rvv.4.1.1, 2026-05-31.

title: F4 design reconciliation: align wildcard_corpus.yml grammar with the shipped Permission + CapabilityGate matchers (or vice versa)
description: BLOCKS wild-rvv.1.2.1 (F4 anti-drift smoke spec). The shared lib/wild/schemas/wildcard_corpus.yml (Role 4 PR-D) and the two consuming matchers never agreed: corpus = ::-segment grammar with 8 forms + boundary semantics (direct-child User::*, single-parent *::Admin, recursive User::**, !negation, middle-*); Permission's WildcardMatcher = .-dotted naive *->. * glob with no segment awareness; CapabilityGate = exact-match only (no capability wildcards, * is caller-only). Real capability names are dotted/flat, not ::-segmented. THREE options the architect must choose between: (a) CORPUS IS SPEC — rework Permission's matcher to honor segment boundaries + give CapabilityGate a real wildcard matcher implementing the same grammar (large behavior change; CapGate currently has none by design — it may be correct that CapGate does exact-match only); (b) CODE IS TRUTH — rewrite the corpus to the actual .-dotted glob grammar both could share, dropping the ::/recursive/negation forms that nothing implements; (c) SCOPE THE FENCE — accept that CapGate does exact-match (no capability wildcards) and that only Permission pattern-matches; rewrite corpus in dotted notation + scope 1.2.1 to Permission only, documenting that CapGate is intentionally exact-match. Recommendation leans (c)+(b): the corpus over-specified a Ruby-constant grammar that doesn't match the dotted capability namespace, and CapGate's exact-match is arguably correct (grants name explicit capabilities). Council F4 intent was 'the two must not DISAGREE on what counts as a wildcard' — if CapGate has no wildcards, there is nothing to disagree about, and the fence is Permission-internal. Needs sign-off (rich-hickey-reviewer for the schema-as-data call + the original F4 council narrative). Source: Role 6 PR-3 investigation, 2026-05-31.
close_reason: Resolved via option (c)+(b) 'code is truth + scope the fence', rich-hickey-reviewer SIGN-OFF. PR #34 (merged d7f2de4). CapabilityGate documented + spec-pinned as exact-symbol-match by design (no capability-name wildcards; caller-* is a different axis) -> F4 'must not disagree' satisfied vacuously. title: Decide-or-cut the inert on_evaluation_error knob + unraised CapabilityGate::EvaluationError class
description: Discovered during wild-rvv.4.1.1 (F2 ordering spec). Relatedly, Wild::CapabilityGate::EvaluationError is declared in the error hierarchy (error.rb:60) and documented as 'F2 — never silent' but is NEVER RAISED anywhere in lib: evaluate unconditionally fails closed (deny + emit), ignoring the knob. DECIDE: (a) WIRE :hard_fail to actually raise EvaluationError (after emitting the audit event — the emit-then-raise ordering the original 4.1.1 bead framing assumed), giving callers an opt-in raising mode distinct from the default deny mode; OR (b) CUT both the knob and the unraised class, documenting the gate as unconditionally fail-closed-deny. Recommendation leans (a) IF a consumer wants raise-on-eval-error semantics, else (b) per 'no speculative infrastructure' (wild-0e0 precedent). Either way the stale 'raised when...' docstring at error.rb:57-60 must be reconciled. Source: wild-rvv.4.1.1 investigation 2026-05-31.

Armstrong F2 gate (wild-rvv.4.1.1) added two acceptance criteria for whichever option is chosen:
(F1/async-durability) If the audit writer ever becomes ASYNC (enqueues a job / hands to a thread and returns before the write lands), the emit-before-return ordering spec NO LONGER proves durability ('write returned' != 'write durable'). Add a durability/fsync invariant then. The ordering spec docstring now documents this scope boundary.
(F4/inert-knob) DONE in the 4.1.1 PR: the on_evaluation_error config site now carries an inline 'CURRENTLY INERT' warning so no operator infers raise semantics from the :hard_fail default. When the knob is finally wired or cut, remove that warning. error.rb EvaluationError docstring also already states DECLARED-but-NOT-RAISED.
Related sibling finding filed separately as wild-0c3 (dark-audit ALLOW posture).
Needs decision (review wave 2026-08-25): (a) wire on_evaluation_error :hard_fail to raise Wild::CapabilityGate::EvaluationError after the audit event, or (b) delete the knob + the unraised class and document the gate as unconditionally fail-closed-deny (fix 003-AT-ARCH:81,107). title: Enforce the wildcard corpus non_matches-non-empty-except-universal invariant in the schema spec instead of a comment

The corpus header (lib/wild/schemas/wildcard_corpus.yml) declares that every entry's non_matches must be non-empty except the universal '*' pattern, but spec/wild/schemas/wildcard_corpus_spec.rb only asserts matches is non-empty — the non_matches rule lives in prose, enforced nowhere. title: Pin the Evaluator-never-raises contract with a Gate-rescue test (Armstrong F2 fast-follow)

title: Centralize wildcard *detection* (include?('*')) into WildcardMatcher.wildcard? so the grammar lives in one module
description: Hickey F4 gate Finding 4 (non-blocking, P3). Wildcard MATCHING is correctly centralized in Wild::Analyzers::Permission::Analyzers::WildcardMatcher.matches?, but wildcard DETECTION ('is this string a pattern at all?') is a bare capabilities.include?('*') duplicated across at least 5 sites: models/grant.rb#wildcard_capabilities, consistency_analyzer.rb, shadow_analyzer.rb, orphan_analyzer.rb, and WildcardMatcher#matches? itself. Today detection and matching agree because both key on the '*' literal, but the day the grammar gains an escape (e.g. backslash-star as a literal star) include?('*') becomes wrong in 5 places simultaneously and the F4 corpus won't catch it (it fences matching, not detection). Fix: add WildcardMatcher.wildcard?(pattern) = pattern.include?('*'); route all 5 sites through it so the grammar (detection + matching) lives in one module. Not an F4 blocker — same concept expressed 5 times.
